issues.legal_issue: A successor tenant cannot be evicted for unlawful subletting committed by the predecessor from whom the tenancy was inherited.
material_facts: The tenant inherited the tenancy after his father died.
The father had created a sub-tenancy before the tenant inherited the tenancy.
The tenant did not create a sub-tenancy after becoming the tenant.
The eviction application relied on the sub-tenancy created by the father.
issues.conclusion: The predecessor’s alleged subletting could not make the successor tenant liable for eviction; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(2)(ii)(a) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960 makes the tenant sought to be evicted liable for the specified subletting. The provision is penal in effect and must be strictly construed: the tenant’s own contravention is required, and liability cannot be based on a predecessor’s conduct. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: rent_eviction_for_subletting and tenancy_inherited_from_predecessor and predecessor_created_subtenancy and successor_did_not_create_subtenancy

predicates.rent_eviction_for_subletting: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant on the ground of unlawful subletting.
predicates.tenancy_inherited_from_predecessor: The tenant acquired the tenancy by succession from a predecessor.
predicates.predecessor_created_subtenancy: The predecessor created the sub-tenancy while holding the tenancy.
predicates.successor_did_not_create_subtenancy: The successor did not create a sub-tenancy while holding the tenancy.

issues.definition: When eviction is sought for subletting created by a predecessor, and the successor did not create a sub-tenancy, the successor is not evictable for the predecessor’s conduct.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord seeking eviction for unlawful subletting must establish that the lease did not permit subletting and that the subletting lacked the landlord’s written consent.
material_facts: The sub-tenancy was created by the tenant’s father many years before the eviction application.
Neither the landlord nor the successor tenant had personal knowledge of the original lease terms or whether written consent had been given.
A sub-tenant openly occupied part of the premises for many years without objection or a possession action.
There was no direct or circumstantial evidence that the lease barred subletting or that the subletting lacked written consent.
issues.conclusion: The landlord had not established an unlawful sub-tenancy and could not obtain eviction on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(2)(ii)(a) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960 applies where the lease confers no right to sublet and the subletting is without the landlord’s written consent. The landlord must establish the statutory conditions for eviction. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: rent_eviction_for_subletting and subtenancy_created and not evidence_lease_barred_subletting and not evidence_subletting_lacked_written_consent

predicates.rent_eviction_for_subletting: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant on the ground of unlawful subletting.
predicates.subtenancy_created: A tenant or predecessor created a sub-tenancy in the rented premises.
predicates.evidence_lease_barred_subletting: Evidence establishes that the lease did not permit the tenant to sublet.
predicates.evidence_subletting_lacked_written_conse: Evidence establishes that the landlord did not give written consent to the subletting.

issues.definition: If eviction is sought for a sub-tenancy but the evidence establishes neither that the lease barred subletting nor that written consent was absent, the unlawful-subletting ground is not established.
